# 10 — Skeletons, Rigging & Facial

Skeleton templates, sockets and facial shape-key sets. They're defined once in `tools/characters/skeletons.py`, which both this chapter and the Blender toolkit read.

**Conventions:** characters **face −Y**, up is +Z, the character's **left is +X** (Blender/Rigify convention; note that building parts use front = +X). Rest pose is **A-pose** (arms 45° down). Bone names follow the UE5 mannequin so animations retarget directly.

| `SOCKET_WeaponL` | `hand_l` | Off-hand item, flashlight, shield |
| `SOCKET_Back` | `spine_04` | Backpack, jetpack, back-slung weapon |
| `SOCKET_HipR` | `pelvis` | Holster |
| `SOCKET_HipL` | `pelvis` | Tool loop (Ada's wrench) |
| `SOCKET_Helmet` | `head` | Helmet / hat attach (head bone origin) |
| `SOCKET_HelmetLight` | `head` | Helmet lamp |
| `SOCKET_ChestLight` | `spine_05` | Chest lamp, radio |
| `SOCKET_WristPad` | `lowerarm_l` | Wrist pad screen (story calls) |
| `SOCKET_Camera1P` | `head` | First-person camera (eye midpoint) |

Sockets are empties parented to their bone in Blender and are exported to the `.meta.json` sidecar; the engine creates skeletal-mesh sockets from it.

## Rigging rules

1. **Deform bones only** carry weights; `ik_*` bones are non-deform but exported (UE5 compatibility).
2. **Max influences:** 8 for Hero/Main/Secondary/Boss, 4 for Crowd, enemies and creatures. Weights normalized.
3. **Twist bones** carry 50% of the forearm and upper-arm roll; never weight the hand to the lowerarm twist.
4. **Facial motion** is shape keys plus `jaw` and `eye_l/r` bones; no other facial bones in the shipping skeleton.
5. **Extra bones** (Bloom attach, jiggle sacs, prosthetic fingers, armor plates) are children of standard bones, named in lowercase with a clear prefix (`bloom_`, `sac_`, `plate_`, `claw_`, `tendril_`), so animation retargeting ignores them.
6. **Outfits and hair** are separate skinned meshes on the same armature; each has its own LODs.
